newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends weaker on light spec selling.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends weaker on light spec selling.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled weaker and at the day's lows as speculators continued to pressure the market, floor sources said.

The selling accelerated at the end of the session, once the March contract fell below 10.80. But prices remained well-within the foreseen trading range between resistance at 11.10 and support at 10.60 cents, for the March contract.
Volume remained light, estimated at a light 11,305 lots.
March closed 0.11 weaker at 10.78, having ranged from 10.93 to 10.76. The back months finished 0.09 to 0.06 lower.
Dealers had expected prices to at least hold some of the sharp gains made Monday, if not crawl slightly higher. They said prices were still oversold from recent losses.
Additionally, E. D. and F. Man, which took the total 4,121 lots, would probably not encounter obstacles in placing the sugar, a trader said.
Today's close signals weakness Tuesday, dealers said.
Steady exports out of Brazil is likely to continue to cast a bearish light on the fundamental picture.
LIFFE white sugar futures also ended the day weaker on continued liquidation, but trade buying buoyed prices from their lows. December finished at $322.50 a tonne, down $2.10.
